concepts.title: Determinant of a Square Matrix
concepts.definition: Each square matrix carries exactly one attached number, denoted det A or |A|; only square matrices get one, and |A| here names the determinant, never a modulus. A one by one matrix [a] has determinant a.
concepts.formula: det A = |A| = the single number attached to a square matrix A
concepts.key_idea: Determinant is a matrix-to-number function defined on square matrices only.

concepts.title: Expansion of a Third Order Determinant
concepts.definition: A three by three determinant breaks into three second order pieces: each entry of the chosen row (or column) multiplies the smaller determinant left after deleting that entry's row and column, with signs alternating plus, minus, plus.
concepts.key_idea: Expanding along any row or column yields the same number; pick the line with the most zeros.

concepts.title: Determinant of a Scalar Multiple
concepts.definition: Multiplying every entry of an order-n square matrix by k multiplies its determinant by k raised to n, since each of the n rows donates one factor of k.
concepts.key_idea: An order-n scaling contributes k to the power n, not k itself.

concepts.definition: Half the magnitude of a determinant assembled from the three vertex coordinates equals the triangle's area; taking the magnitude keeps the area positive whichever way the corners wind.

concepts.title: Collinearity by Zero Determinant
concepts.definition: Three points lie on one straight line exactly when the determinant built from their coordinates works out to zero, since the triangle they would form then has no area.
concepts.formula: x1 * (y2 - y3) + x2 * (y3 - y1) + x3 * (y1 - y2) = 0 for collinear points
concepts.key_idea: Zero area from the vertex determinant is the collinearity test.

concepts.title: Minor of an Element
concepts.definition: Strike out the row and the column holding a chosen entry; the smaller determinant left behind is that entry's minor, and it has order one less than the original.

concepts.title: Cofactor with Alternating Sign
concepts.definition: A cofactor is the matching minor carrying a sign: plus when the entry's row and column indices add to an even total, minus when that total is odd.
concepts.key_idea: Cofactor equals signed minor; the sign alternates by position parity.

concepts.title: Cofactor Expansion Identity
concepts.definition: Pairing each entry of one row or column with its own cofactor and adding reproduces the determinant, while pairing a row's entries with a different row's cofactors always totals zero.
concepts.key_idea: Own-row cofactor products rebuild the determinant; foreign-row pairings cancel to zero.

concepts.title: Adjoint of a Matrix
concepts.definition: Replace every entry of the square matrix by its cofactor, then transpose the resulting grid; that transposed cofactor grid is the adjoint of the matrix.
concepts.formula: adj A = transpose of the cofactor grid of A

concepts.title: Invertibility by Singularity Test
concepts.definition: A square matrix is singular when its determinant is zero and non-singular otherwise; only in the non-singular case does an inverse exist, given by the adjoint divided by the determinant.
concepts.formula: A_inverse = adj A / det A when det A is not 0
concepts.key_idea: Non-zero determinant is the exact licence for an inverse to exist.

concepts.title: Determinant of the Adjoint
concepts.definition: For a square matrix of order n, the adjoint's own determinant equals the original determinant raised to the power n minus one.

concepts.title: Matrix Method for a Linear System
concepts.definition: Pack the equations as AX = B; when the coefficient matrix is non-singular, the solution column follows as the inverse of A multiplied by B, giving the unique answer.
